grain.truth: In the sales table one row is one rep for FY2025, with a Units and Revenue pair per quarter; subtotal and total rows are not reps.

other_grains.truth: One row is one product; one column is one month.

facts.truth: Regional Sales has a two-row header (rows 3 and 4): quarter labels Q1 to Q4 and FY Total are merged across a Units and a Revenue column.
Region is written only on the first rep row of each block and applies to the rows below it.
Rows labeled East Subtotal, West Subtotal, Central Subtotal and Grand Total (row 19) are formulas; summing all rows double counts.
A second table, Returns by Region (header row 21), sits below the sales table after one blank row, with its own Total row.
A note in row 27 says West Q3 excludes the Driftwood account, which moved to Key Accounts in August.
Revenue figures are in thousands of dollars ($000); Units are units shipped. Nothing in the sheet says so.
Monthly Units is a pivoted (wide) export: one row per product, one column per month of 2025, plus a Total column and a Grand Total row.
FY Total columns are formulas adding the four quarters.
The owner wants the data in long format to feed a dashboard.

owner_brief:
You are Tom Lindqvist, sales analyst at Kestrel Outdoor Gear, a maker of packs, tents and camp gear. You maintain messy_multitable.xlsx.

Regional Sales: rows are reps grouped by region (East, West, Central). You only type the region on the first rep of each group; it applies to the rows below. Each quarter has a Units column and a Revenue column under a merged quarter heading. Revenue is in thousands of dollars; everyone on the team knows that, so it is not written anywhere. Units are units shipped. The subtotal rows and the Grand Total are formulas. FY Total adds the four quarters.

Below the sales table, after a blank row, is a second small table: returns in units by region and quarter, with a Total row. Under that is a note: West Q3 excludes the Driftwood account, which moved to Key Accounts in August.

Monthly Units is a pivot export of units shipped by product and month for 2025, with a Total column and a Grand Total row.

Your goal: get all of this into a clean long format for a dashboard.

Answer only what you are asked, briefly. If a question is not covered here, say "not sure".

eval_questions.q: What was total FY2025 revenue across all reps, in dollars?
eval_questions.a: $2,901,600.00. The Revenue columns are in thousands ($2,901.6 thousand), and the subtotal and Grand Total rows must not be added again.

eval_questions.q: How many sales reps are in the Regional Sales table?
eval_questions.a: 11 reps (subtotal and total rows are not reps).

eval_questions.q: Which region had the highest Q4 revenue, and how much in dollars?
How many units did Grant, L. sell in Q2?
What were total FY returns in units?
eval_questions.a: 286 units, from the second table (Returns by Region) stacked below the sales table.

eval_questions.q: What were East region FY units?

eval_questions.a: The note below the tables says West Q3 excludes the Driftwood account, which moved to Key Accounts in August.
eval_questions.value: Note: West Q3 excludes the Driftwood account, which moved to Key Accounts in August. Figures from the regional close files.

eval_questions.q: What was the West return rate (FY returned units over FY units sold)?
On Monthly Units, which product sold the most units in 2025, and which month had the most units overall?
eval_questions.a: Cairn Trekking Poles with 1565 units; June 2025 had the most units overall (1460).

eval_questions.q: How many rows would Monthly Units have in long format (one row per product per month)?
eval_questions.a: 120 (10 products x 12 months; the Grand Total row and Total column drop out).

region label only on the first row of each block
3 subtotal rows and a Grand Total row (formulas)
second table stacked below after a blank row
free-text note cell under the tables
